title: The Girl Who Trod on a Loaf

keywords: the girl who trod on a loaf
full_text:
There was once a proud, beautiful girl named Inger, whose vanity made her heart as hard as stone. She was sent to carry a large loaf of white bread to her poor mother in the country.

Reaching a muddy ditch, Inger did not wish to soil her fine new shoes. So she tossed the loaf of bread into the mud to use as a stepping stone!

The moment her foot touched the bread, she sank straight down into the earth! Down she plunged into the dark, slimy subterranean kingdom of the Marsh Woman, where toads and snakes crawled over her limbs.

She was turned into a stiff, frozen stone statue, standing in the mire, tormented by the memories of her cruelty. Passersby in the world above told her story as a warning.

One day, a little girl heard the tale and wept bitter tears of pity: "Poor Inger! May God have mercy on her soul!"

The tear of pure, unselfish pity fell into the underworld, melting Inger's stone heart. Inger wept tears of genuine remorse, and was transformed into a little gray bird that flew across the fields gathering breadcrumbs for starving birds, until her debt was redeemed and she ascended into the golden light of heaven.
moral: Pride that scorns the bread of life sinks into the mud; humble repentance alone unlocks redemption.
